Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

cmrdesign (development version)

Bug fixes

  • cmr_multiarm() and rectangle_multiarm() no longer fail when a treatment arm label starts with “v”, such as "variant_a" or "v1". Arm labels are never renamed. The v prefix is removed only from variance names of the form v0, v1, and so on.
  • cmr_stratified() and rectangle_stratified() accept stratum labels that contain a colon, such as "age:18-30".
  • method = "auto" looks at the raw outcome values in multi-arm and stratified designs, as it already did in two-arm designs and as documented. A two-valued outcome that is not coded 0/1 is treated as bounded in every design.
  • cmr_plan() no longer classifies a pilot as inside the viability band when the band is empty.
  • A stratum that receives no sample has an NA treatment margin, not NaN.
  • cmr_multiarm_from_rectangle() accepts a matrix rectangle without row names and labels its rows 0, 1, and so on.

Changes in behavior

  • pilot_viability_band() and cmr_plan() default to strict_upper = FALSE. A pilot equal to the design-only break-even cap is feasible, which reproduces the band m_act <= m <= cap and the worked examples of the accompanying paper. Set strict_upper = TRUE for the 0.1.0 behavior.
  • General multi-arm and stratified rectangles are solved by a barrier Newton method with a certified optimality gap. U_CMR can be slightly smaller than in 0.1.0, by up to about 2e-4 in relative terms in our checks. diagnostics$solver reads "barrier_newton", diagnostics$optimality_gap bounds the distance to the minimax value, and a warning is raised if the solver does not reach its tolerance. The multi-start search of 0.1.0 is the fallback and remains available with solver_control = list(barrier = FALSE).
  • With method = "auto", raw 0/1 outcomes, and normalize = TRUE with support bounds other than [0, 1], a warning says that normalization was skipped. An explicit method = "bernoulli" is applied to the normalized outcome.
  • A constant outcome under data-dependent normalization is mapped to 0.5, as in the Python package. It was mapped to 0.

New features

  • A scalar beta is accepted by cmr_two_arm(), rectangle_two_arm(), cmr_proxy(), and the index mode of cmr_multiple_outcomes().
  • cmr_plan() returns two_thirds_status, which says where the two-thirds-power pilot size falls relative to the viability band.
  • regret(), variance_objective(), oracle_variance(), assign_neyman(), coverage_indicator(), certificate_valid(), saving_vs_balance(), and share_of_oracle_gain() gain scale = "nonnegative" for auditing cmr_unbounded() results.
  • Compact print() methods for pilot plans, viability bands, and confidence rectangles.
  • Errors raised while processing one arm, cell, or outcome name it.

Documentation

  • The examples of the main functions use pilots large enough to move the allocation, and explain the balanced result that a small pilot returns.

cmrdesign 0.1.0

CRAN release: 2026-08-05

First CRAN release of cmrdesign, published on 2026-08-05.

  • Added applied Conditional Minimax Regret rules for two-arm, unbounded two-arm, shared-control multi-arm, stratified, multiple-outcome, and proxy outcome designs.
  • Added pilot/main-wave sample-size planning tools from Appendix E of the accompanying paper.
  • Added R/Python cross-language fixtures, reference validation, vignettes, and compact print/summary methods for core CMR results.
  • Added realize_allocation() to turn CMR target shares into integer main-wave counts and recompute the rounded-design certificate when possible.
  • Added allocation cross-language fixtures and vignette/examples coverage for integer count realization.
  • Hardened realize_allocation() input validation for named length-one targets, fixed stratum counts, zero-count realized arms, and certificate recomputation diagnostics.
  • Maurer–Pontil bounded-outcome fits now report the raw Bessel sample variance in vhat and keep projected unit-interval variances in the method-specific statistic$projected_vhat field.
  • Added explicit warnings when normalize = TRUE uses pilot min/max support bounds, clarifying that this convenience path is exploratory rather than finite-sample guarantee-bearing.
